solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Magnificent items referring to type of melon

blocks.note: re is the short word meaning concerning or about
the Galia is a variety of sweet melon

explanation.surface: Someone describing splendid things by comparison with a particular melon.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the splendid emblems of royalty or office, such as crowns and sceptres, so grand ceremonial objects.

clue.text: Blackpool, say, put in order again?

blocks.note: first meaning: a seaside holiday town
second meaning: read as ..., to sort once more

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Blackpool has been rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a traditional seaside holiday town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination, and re-sort means to arrange in order a second time.

clue.text: Noble ignored, as vulgar

indicators.note: vulgar means debased or corrupted, as a vulgar tongue is a corruption of a classical one

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is snubbed for being coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: Noble and vulgar look like opposite descriptions of a person; the first is the definition, the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means imposing or magnificent in scale, which matches noble in the sense of stately.

clue.text: Grub with last of pepper in very hot stuff

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the following word
in places the single letter inside the substance named after it

blocks.note: lava is molten rock
final letter of pepper

explanation.surface: Food spiced with a final dash of pepper in a fiery dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub looks like slang for food, matching the pepper and hot stuff, but it means an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature form of an insect, and a grub is a larva of a beetle or similar.

clue.text: Athenian building a farm store up having gathered in harvest

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
gathering something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a silo stores grain on a farm
a crop is what is harvested

explanation.surface: A Greek barn holding the gathered harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed farm store wraps the harvest, and the A stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the ancient citadel on the hill above Athens, crowned by the Parthenon.

clue.text: Skilled worker in braggart is a narcissist

indicators.note: in says the wanted word sits inside the following run of letters

blocks.note: found spanning the end of braggart, all of is and a, and the start of narcissist

explanation.surface: A craftsman is spotted among the boastful and self-obsessed.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson, a manual worker trained in a particular trade.

clue.text: Meeting place in coast's 1 down?

indicators.note: the answer at 1 down can be read as put in order again, so these letters are re-sorted

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gathering spot is at a seaside resort on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference looks like it means a holiday town; it is the re-sort reading, an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, and a race meeting is held there, so it is a meeting place.

clue.text: Very high price to model in standard measure

indicators.note: in places the figure inside the measure that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
par is the standard or normal level
a doll is a model of a person

explanation.surface: A fashion model is paid a fortune by the usual yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying top dollar is paying the highest possible price for something.

clue.text: Cracking author

blocks.note: first meaning: very fast, as in a cracking pace
second meaning: Jonathan, who wrote Gulliver's Travels

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a great writer; cracking here means quick, and the writer is a specific Irish satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means rapid, as a cracking pace is, and is also the surname of the satirist Jonathan.

clue.text: Scratching head, one tiny bewildered figure

indicators.note: scratching out the head means striking off the first letter
bewildered means confused, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: one without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled little person scratching their head.
explanation.walkthrough: Scratching head looks like a sign of puzzlement; it removes the head of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, and figure is a common crossword word for a number.

clue.text: Move round across a step

indicators.note: one thing spread across another straddles it, holding it in the middle

blocks.note: to stir is to move a spoon round in a pot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance instruction: shift round, crossing over a step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight of them.

clue.text: Party where nice toper gets sozzled

indicators.note: someone sozzled is drunk and muddled, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A party at which a pleasant drunkard ends up plastered.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal party, such as one held after a wedding.

clue.text: A walkover for Oscar nominees?

blocks.note: surface reading: an easy victory, as if the nominees were sure to win
setter's reading: something the film stars literally walk over on arrival at the ceremony

explanation.surface: Suggesting the Academy Awards are an easy win for everyone shortlisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Walkover usually means an easy win; here it is read literally as a thing walked over, the carpet laid for stars arriving at a premiere or awards night.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpet laid for celebrities at the Oscars is a strip they literally walk along into the ceremony.

clue.text: Eight nos. cut, lest odds cut

indicators.note: cutting the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and so on

blocks.note: the even letters of nos cut lest

explanation.surface: A cryptic memo about trimming numbers, for fear the odds are cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder reads like abbreviated instructions; the run n-o-s-c-u-t-l-e-s-t, minus every odd letter, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, such as eight musicians or eight bits.

clue.text: One swimmer from Dover?

blocks.note: first meaning: only, single, as in the only survivor
second meaning: a flatfish, the Dover variety being the famous one

explanation.surface: A single cross-Channel swimmer setting off from the port of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover suggests a Channel swimmer; it is the Dover sole, a prized flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, and is also the name of a flat sea fish.

clue.text: Ultimately all square ie, producing — this?

definitions.text: Ultimately all square ie, producing — this?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word
producing means making something new out of the material given

blocks.note: final letter of all
the remaining letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A late goal leaves the match level, and the clue asks what did it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a late score that makes it all square is exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: An equaliser is the goal that levels the score in a match, leaving the teams all square.

clue.text: Apathetic when register lost?

blocks.note: a register is a list of names
the suffix meaning lacking or without

explanation.surface: Someone becomes indifferent after the attendance register goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless describes someone lacking energy or interest, which is apathy.

clue.text: Vicious, say, figure punched by left getting shiner

indicators.note: something punched has a hole knocked in it, with the puncher left inside

blocks.note: Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bass player
eight is a number
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A violent figure throws a left punch and the victim gets a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Shiner suggests a black eye from the punch; it is just something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp on a vehicle or a window beside a door, either way something that shines.

clue.text: Watch over vipers, use snakes

indicators.note: snakes is a verb here, meaning winds about, so the letters twist into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A herpetologist's instruction to keep an eye on dangerous reptiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes looks like more reptiles beside vipers; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to oversee, keeping watch over people or work.

clue.text: Disgusted by seed in cherry

indicators.note: in places one item within the other, as the stone sits within the fruit

blocks.note: cherry is a shade of red
pulses are edible seeds such as lentils or peas

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at biting into a stone in a cherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Cherry is a colour here, not a fruit, so the seed goes inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repulsed is to be revolted or filled with disgust.

clue.text: Exercise on theological teachings is ready

blocks.note: RI is religious instruction, the old school subject
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A study of religious doctrine is now ready.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed after in an across clue, so the exercise follows the teachings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe fruit is ready to eat, and something ripe for action is ready for it.

clue.text: State of shock seeing leader of union in terrible strop

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
terrible means awful, so the next word is badly mangled
in places the single letter inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: a strop is a fit of bad temper; its letters are rearranged
first letter of union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is stunned to see a dreadful tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is British slang for a sulk or fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state of near-unconsciousness, the kind brought on by shock.

clue.text: Plug over hole is coming

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the second

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: A plumber's note that the stopper for the drain is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug looks like a bath stopper; it is a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means arrival, from the Latin for coming to, as in the advent of the railways.

clue.text: Flowing locks are down idle teenager's back, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word that precedes it
going back means the letters are read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A lazy adolescent's hair cascades down their back.
explanation.walkthrough: Back seems to be where the hair hangs, but it reverses the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal water flows in and out with the tides, so it is flowing water.

clue.text: Board game is 7 down

blocks.note: first meaning: the pub game of throwing arrows at a dartboard
second meaning: is swift, that is, moves quickly

explanation.walkthrough: Board game suggests chess or Monopoly; it is the game played at a board on the wall. The cross-reference means is quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game played against a circular board, and someone who darts moves rapidly.

clue.text: Vital thing in contract handed over

indicators.note: in puts one item inside the other, as a clause sits inside a document

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal agreement
the liver is a vital organ

explanation.surface: An essential clause is passed over in a legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Vital thing sounds like a key term in a contract; it is a vital organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivered means passed into someone's hands, as goods are handed over.

clue.text: Spin right amid plummet

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece is set inside the other

blocks.note: to dive is to drop steeply
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An aircraft spirals to the right while falling sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin suggests a nosedive, matching plummet; it is a pleasure trip in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a journey in a car, and a spin is an informal word for a short ride.

clue.text: One certainly won't have animals for example transported in commercial vehicle

indicators.note: something transported in a vehicle is carried inside it

blocks.note: a van is a goods vehicle
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A haulier refusing to carry livestock in the delivery lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Have animals looks like owning or carrying them; it means eating them, or any product from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids all animal products, so they never consume meat, dairy or eggs.

clue.text: Dying of cold?

definitions.note: a phrase meaning freezing, as the adjective is used of weather

blocks.note: first meaning: losing one's life, expiring
second meaning: bitterly freezing, in British colloquial use

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one idea, freezing to death; the word covers each half separately, since in British speech it also describes weather that is extremely cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die, and perishing is a colloquial British adjective for bitterly cold weather.

clue.text: Masquerade chaps discussed?

indicators.note: things discussed are spoken out loud, so what matters is the sound of the word

blocks.note: guys are chaps; the spelling changes but the sound stays

explanation.surface: Men in disguise at a masked ball become the talk of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an assumed outward appearance or pretence, which is what a masquerade is.

clue.text: Substitute hit tennis ball again?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stand-in player on the bench
second meaning: read as ..., to serve once more

explanation.surface: A replacement player being asked to take another serve in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a back-up player, and re-serve splits into a prefix and the tennis stroke that starts a point.

clue.text: Brown kissing bloke — that's just touching

indicators.note: things kissing are in contact, so the two parts sit side by side

blocks.note: tan is a shade of brown
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Someone moved by the sight of a man named Brown kissing another man.
explanation.walkthrough: Touching seems to mean moving or sweet; in geometry it means meeting a curve at one point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line that meets a curve at exactly one point without crossing it.
